name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Build a self-review loop where every prompt update triggers an automated review of the same task batch that triggered the update. This keeps quality high by catching regressions immediately, not after 500 new tasks pile up. Trade-off: we accept slower updates for individual prompts because the review step adds latency, but the trade is worth it to prevent bad changes from spreading.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just slower updates—it’s that testing 500 tasks after every prompt tweak guarantees we’ll drown in false positives. A better alternative: batch prompt updates by semantic similarity, then test only the affected task clusters. Settle it by running a controlled A/B where we compare regression rates between immediate vs. batched reviews over 100 updates.
